trigger: merging the branch with the new GATE_PARITY_NO_GATE_ALLOWED entry (MAX 13 to 14) and ADR residual (c) saying a tracker is 'yet to be filed'
policy_floor: ADR-1005 exception-ledger rule: new entry needs a tracking issue (accepted ADR normative requirement)
summary: ADR-1005 ledger rule (~line 912) requires a reason, a tracking issue and a ruling for a new exception entry; the entry had a reason and a ruling but no issue. Also raised by consistency-auditor and compliance-officer. Fixed: issue #6984 filed with the owner's go, cited in the ADR residual (c) and in the reason string (exception:#6984 revisit:2026-11-30), revisit date commented on the issue.
classification_rationale: a required tracking issue was missing; the ADR rule is a normative requirement so it gates as a policy floor

trigger: audit-off deployment: McpRig always wired audit_fn so a mutation making try_persist_audit return false for an empty callback passed every test
summary: No MCP case with an empty audit callback; audit_persisted must stay true when no sink is wired. Fixed: McpRig gained audit_wired and a case asserts audit_persisted:true.
classification_rationale: a documented behaviour had no test

trigger: RBAC on, an OIDC principal with a durable Administrator grant: docs said SSO-only principals read may_not
summary: An OIDC login provisions an active auth.users row (upsert_sso_identity), so the docs' blanket 'SSO-only reads may_not' was wrong for a granted OIDC administrator. Fixed by naming the real may_not cases (SAML, SCIM-deactivated, JIT, group-held, OIDC without a grant) in the docs, OpenAPI and MCP description.
classification_rationale: a documentation claim contradicted the provisioning code

trigger: a customer admin or agentic worker reads the corrected sentence 'an OIDC administrator who holds the grant reads may' as a supported path
summary: No production route can write a grant for an oidc:<iss>#<sub> principal id (assignment routes reject the charset; direct SQL only; provisioning is fail-soft), so the fix-pass-1 wording described a state operators cannot reach. Independently raised by security-guardian and docs-writer. Fixed: docs say an OIDC principal reads may_not in practice today and what would change that; two contradicted older sentences scoped.
classification_rationale: the previous fix's wording overclaimed a reachable state

trigger: enabled:true with unconfirmed:true and a caller with no Administrator grant row
summary: Prose said an account with no Administrator grant row reads administrator:unconfirmed whenever the view is unconfirmed; that holds only for a stale cached OFF (rbac_enforcement_label returns kEnabled for a stale ON, so the account reads may_not). Found again independently by security-guardian and consistency-auditor at gate 8 of the first run, and a new test pins the stale-on case. Fixed everywhere (header, OpenAPI, docs, ADR).
classification_rationale: comment and docs contradicted rbac_enforcement_label and the predicate

trigger: RBAC off, degraded cached view, local admin with no Administrator grant row
summary: Docs said administrator is independent of the cached view / never forced to unconfirmed; the predicate reads the cached enforcement label to choose its durable source and maps a degraded label plus an absent grant to unavailable. Fixed: builder header and docs reworded; pinned by test.
classification_rationale: comments and docs contradicted the predicate

trigger: REST audit write fails
summary: The REST audit-failure 503 carried no retry_after_ms while the store-unavailable 503 and the MCP twin did. Fixed (A4ErrorOpts retry_after_ms = kMcpStoreFaultRetryMs) and pinned by a test assertion after quality-engineer, architect, cpp-safety and consistency-auditor each found the assertion missing.
classification_rationale: an advertised A4 contract was not delivered on one path

trigger: a client reads the RBAC tag guide or the OpenAPI GET text
summary: RBAC guide still said MCP tokens and engines are refused on 'enforcement' calls and 'four calls only read'; OpenAPI said a refused call writes no audit row although a service-scoped refusal writes a denied row. Fixed.
classification_rationale: served documentation contradicted the new GET

trigger: rolling upgrade: an older replica audits get_rbac_enforcement as result=denied detail=unknown tool
summary: Upgrade notes said only 404 / unknown tool. Also raised by unhappy-path (UP-7) and sre. Fixed in upgrading.md, rest-api.md and mcp.md (written as 'expected', not observed).
classification_rationale: an upgrade-relevant behaviour was undocumented

trigger: an agentic worker follows 're-read in a few seconds' and polls the audited read
summary: The manual never told a client that each call writes an audit row (two on MCP). Fixed: cadence sentence (poll no faster than 5000 ms) in rest-api.md, mcp.md, the MCP description and the OpenAPI text.
classification_rationale: partial documentation of a shipped behaviour

trigger: a later auditor request for access-monitoring evidence
summary: The SOC 2 inventory listed the toggle audit but not the new rbac.enforcement.read verb or its documented gaps. Fixed: bullet added (no tamper-evidence claim).
classification_rationale: a required evidence document was not updated

trigger: an auditor samples rbac.enforcement.read rows and reads administrator= as effective authority
summary: The recorded verdict is advisory (cached per replica, excludes group-held and JIT authority). Fixed, plus principal_role clarified as the effective authorized role, not a credential signal.
classification_rationale: the audit-log row omitted that the recorded verdict is advisory, which an auditor needs to read the evidence correctly

trigger: regime_authority coerces an absent rbac_meta row to false: the cached-on section would read may_not and still pass
summary: The new rbac_meta-row-deleted case compared the hint with itself. Fixed: both sections assert administrator == unconfirmed and the audit detail.
classification_rationale: test strength

trigger: the rbac_enabled row is absent on a replica
summary: No route test for a missing rbac_enabled row (a non-canonical value is unwritable: CHECK constraint). Fixed: a case asserts a 200 with unconfirmed:true after the stale-serve bound, never a 5xx. The missing alert for this state is tracked by #6461 (evidence commented).
classification_rationale: an unhappy path had no test

trigger: Postgres slow but alive, or pool saturated, while authenticated principals poll the read
summary: The hint's two reads and the audit INSERT take leases outside the circuit breaker; bounded by the 0.5 s pool fast-fail and fail-closed (REST 503 / MCP audit_persisted:false), not new in kind (any lease-taking route). Not measured; chaos scenarios CH-3 deferred.
classification_rationale: behaviour under a partial fault is unmeasured

trigger: any authenticated credential polls the audited read at the per-IP limiter ceiling (100/s)
summary: About 8.6M REST / 17M MCP audit rows per day from one IP, 365-day retention, reaper deletes only expired rows. I5(b) HIGH not met (concurrent pooled INSERT, not serialised; rate-bounded; the same lever exists via denied-permission rows, #1643) and the owner ruled 'audit every read'. Throttle / memo and bytes-per-row measurement tracked by #7022.
classification_rationale: an owner-ruled behaviour whose volume is unbounded

trigger: get_principal_roles_checked or regime_authority fails: administrator:unconfirmed with no log or metric
summary: The sibling list_all_principal_roles_checked counts degrade; these two reads do not. Tracked by #7023.
classification_rationale: an observability gap

trigger: the HTML fragment's enforcement_state_fn drifts from the shared builder
summary: The fragment lambda is pinned by text tests and not constructible in a unit test, so no agreement test exists; the fragment and /api/v1/me also read the same state unaudited. Tracked by #7024.
classification_rationale: design follow-up

trigger: a later change to rbac_enforcement_read.hpp does not route to security-guardian by path
summary: The builder is the second production caller of rbac_admin_hint but is not named in the A2/A1 row; the file is shared with the RBAC 4996 session and has ~30 characters of headroom, so it was deliberately not edited. Tracked by #7026.
classification_rationale: routing table gap

trigger: the real AuditStore INSERT blocks (lock_timeout 10 s) or its lease times out
summary: Fail-closed behaviour is pinned only with a mock sink. No fail-open path was found by reading the code. Scenarios CH-2, CH-3, CH-4, CH-5 tracked by #7025.
classification_rationale: coverage gap

trigger: a bad_alloc-class throw inside the GET handler
summary: No try/catch or set_exception_handler in the route; a throw gives an empty-body 500. Platform-wide pattern shared by every route, speculative trigger.
classification_rationale: platform pattern, no concrete trigger

trigger: reading the A5 exception table
summary: The A5 row for #2990 has a revisit-by date (2026-10-31) that is past; mcp.md table row count and a runbook sentence also drifted before this change. Tracked by #7027.
classification_rationale: pre-existing documentation drift

trigger: reading the OpenAPI text, route comment, fragment section, curl examples
summary: Batch of wording fixes: possessive in the OpenAPI text, garbled and over-long route comment, fragment section ambiguity, Cache-Control on the 200 only, bearer curl example and host convention, RBAC guide Audit step. All fixed.
classification_rationale: wording only

trigger: an operator reads the audit-outage alternative during an RBAC-store outage
summary: The named alternatives (gauge, GET /api/v1/me) are cached views that do not report the degraded fail-closed state. Fixed.
classification_rationale: precision

trigger: reading rbac.md list item 3 and the OpenAPI cadence sentence
summary: Item 3 sat under a heading that mislabelled the OIDC case; 'each call writes an audit row' overclaimed for a 401 or 503. Fixed (final commit).
classification_rationale: precision
